title: Pharmaceutical Sample Management — Regulatory Requirements by Region
summary: Comprehensive regulatory requirements for pharmaceutical sample management across US, EU, Japan, and Brazil, covering distribution controls, signature capture, inventory reconciliation, reporting obligations, and CRM configuration implications.

us_pdma.name: Prescription Drug Marketing Act (PDMA) — 21 CFR Part 203
requirements: Complete chain of custody from manufacturer to healthcare provider — every sample must be traceable
Written request from HCP required before sample distribution (can be electronic)
HCP signature at point of receipt — must be captured and retained for 3 years
Annual physical inventory reconciliation for every field representative
Lot tracking with expiration date enforcement — expired samples cannot be distributed
Loss or theft reporting to FDA within 5 business days of discovery
Manufacturer must verify HCP license status before distribution
crm_configuration: Sample Transaction object must capture: HCP identity, products/quantities, lot numbers, signature, timestamp, and GPS coordinates (optional but recommended)
Inventory counting workflow with discrepancy resolution and mandatory reason codes
Sample limit enforcement at the product and rep level — configurable per business rules
Lot management with automatic expiration blocking
Signature capture on mobile device with tamper-evident storage
Reconciliation reports exportable for FDA audit

eu_framework.name: EU Directive 2001/83/EC (as amended) + Country-Specific Implementations
requirements: Each EU member state implements sample distribution rules differently — there is no single EU-wide sample regulation
Germany: maximum one smallest package per product per HCP per visit, maximum two per product per year
France: sample distribution is prohibited for certain drug categories; mandatory reporting to ANSM
Italy: AIFA requires sample request forms and limits per product per HCP
Spain: sample distribution limited to products marketed in the last 2 years with authorized promotional materials
Most EU countries require samples to be marked 'FREE MEDICAL SAMPLE — NOT FOR SALE'
crm_configuration: Country-specific sample limit rules — the target platform must support different limit configurations per country
Sample labeling compliance tracking (free sample marking)
Per-country reporting exports matching local authority requirements
Multi-language sample request form support
Country-level product eligibility rules (some products cannot be sampled in certain countries)

japan_mhlw.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) + JPMA Guidelines
requirements: Samples classified as 'trial-use drugs' with specific handling and documentation requirements
JPMA self-regulatory guidelines limit sample quantities and require detailed distribution logging
MR (Medical Representative) certification must be verified before allowing sample distribution
Lot tracking with Japanese regulatory lot number format
Distribution records must be retained and available for MHLW inspection
crm_configuration: MR certification status validation before sample transactions are allowed
Japanese lot number format support
JPMA-compliant sample quantity limits
Distribution reports in MHLW-required format
Integration point for trial-use drug classification data

brazil_anvisa.name: ANVISA RDC Regulations + CFF Rules
requirements: ANVISA regulates sample distribution as part of pharmaceutical promotion oversight
Nota Fiscal (tax document) required for interstate movement of sample shipments
Samples must be labeled with ANVISA registration number and 'AMOSTRA GRÁTIS' marking
Distribution records must be available for ANVISA inspection
State-level ICMS tax implications for sample logistics
crm_configuration: Nota Fiscal reference field on sample shipment records
ANVISA registration number on product/lot records
Portuguese-language sample forms and reports
State-level compliance tracking for interstate sample movement
ANVISA-specific reporting exports

cross_region_migration_considerations: Source platform sample data structures vary by region — US implementations have different fields and workflows than EU or Japan implementations
Sample transaction history is regulatory data and cannot be selectively migrated — complete history migration is required for all regions
Signature data must be migrated with cryptographic integrity intact — re-signing is not an option
Lot expiration dates must be preserved exactly — timezone handling during migration can shift dates and invalidate lots
Sample limit configurations are the most country-specific part of the CRM — plan separate configuration and testing per country
Reconciliation reports generated from the source platform should be archived before migration and compared against target platform reports post-migration
For multi-country migrations, Phase 1 should include the US market (most mature sample management requirements) to establish the baseline configuration
source: Lumis Knowledge Base — compiled from FDA PDMA (21 CFR 203), EU Directive 2001/83/EC, MHLW guidelines, ANVISA regulations
